arxiv-1509-04529.title: LACUNARY STATISTICAL CONVERGENCE OF ORDER
arxiv-1509-04529.creator: β
arxiv-1509-04529.description: A 2015 arXiv research paper by β. In this paper, we define the spaces N_{\theta}^{\beta}\left(p,F,\Delta^{m}\right), S_{\theta}^{\beta}\left(F,\Delta^{m}\right), w_{p}^{\beta}\left(F,\Delta^{m}\right) for sequences of fuzzy numbers using generalized difference operator \Delta^{m} and a lacunary sequence \theta and give some relations between them, where \beta\in\left(0,1\right] and p>0 . Furthermore, in the last section of paper, some inclusion theorems are presented related to the spaces S_{\theta}^{\beta}\left(F,\Delta^{m}\right) and w_{p}^{\beta}\left(\theta,f,F,\Delta^{m}\right) according to modulus function f .

arxiv-2103-15102.title: Weakly maxitive set functions and their possibility distributions Thanks: We thank two anonymous referees for their helpful suggestions and remarks.
arxiv-2103-15102.creator: Michael Kupper, José M. Zapata
arxiv-2103-15102.description: Abstract . The Shilkret integral with respect to a completely maxitive capacity is fully determined by a possibility distribution. In this paper, we introduce a weaker topological form of maxitivity and show that under this assumption the Shilkret integral is still determined by its possibility distribution for functions that are sufficiently regular.

arxiv-2306-10304.title: Understanding Revision Behavior in Adaptive Writing Support Systems for Education
arxiv-2306-10304.creator: Luca Mouchel Thiemo Wambsganss Paola Mejia-Domenzain, Tanja Käser
arxiv-2306-10304.description: Abstract Revision behavior in adaptive writing support systems is an important and relatively new area of research that can improve the design and effectiveness of these tools, and promote students’ self-regulated learning (SRL). Understanding how these tools are used is key to improving them to better support learners in their writing and learning processes.

arxiv-2407-03522.title: Optimal thresholds and algorithms for a model of multi-modal learning in high dimensions
arxiv-2407-03522.creator: Christian Keup, Lenka Zdeborová
arxiv-2407-03522.description: Abstract This work explores multi-modal inference in a high-dimensional simplified model, analytically quantifying the performance gain of multi-modal inference over that of analyzing modalities in isolation. We present the Bayes-optimal performance and recovery thresholds in a model where the objective is to recover the latent structures from two noisy data matrices with correlated spikes.

pmc-10526923.title: ABCC1, ABCG2 and FOXP3: Predictive Biomarkers of Toxicity from Methotrexate Treatment in Patients Diagnosed with Moderate-to-Severe Psoriasis
pmc-10526923.creator: Cristina Membrive-Jiménez, Sayleth Vieira-Maroun, Noelia Márquez-Pete, Yasmin Cura, Cristina Pérez-Ramírez, Jesús Tercedor-Sánchez, Alberto Jiménez-Morales, María del Carmen Ramírez-Tortosa, Dae Joon Kim
pmc-10526923.description: Background: Methotrexate (MTX) is one of the most extensively used drugs in the treatment of moderate-to-severe psoriasis (PS). However, it frequently must be suspended owing to the toxicity in certain patients. Objective: To evaluate the influence of ABCC1, ABCG2, and FOXP3 in the development of MTX toxicity in PS. Methods: Retrospective cohort study with 101 patients.

pmc-10736793.title: SMOOTHING SPLINE ANOVA MONITORING PHYSICAL ACTIVITY AND FALL RISK IN COMMUNITY-DWELLING OLDER ADULTS
pmc-10736793.creator: Rui Xie, Lulu Chen, Joon-Hyuk Park, Jeffrey Stout, Ladda Thiamwong
pmc-10736793.description: Emerging sensing techniques, which are easily transportable, user-friendly, and cost-effective, may reveal new possibilities in monitoring daily objectively measured physical activity (PA) and fall risk appraisal (FRA) identification. We used a Smoothing Spline Analysis of Variance (SS-ANOVA) to profile the daily PA using accelerometer-based device across FRA groups.

pmc-11446992.title: Longitudinal metabolite and protein trajectories prior to diabetes mellitus diagnosis in Danish blood donors: a nested case–control study
pmc-11446992.creator: Agnete T Lundgaard, David Westergaard, Timo Röder, Kristoffer S Burgdorf, Margit H Larsen, Michael Schwinn, Lise W Thørner, Erik Sørensen, DBDS Genomic Consortium, Kaspar R Nielsen, Henrik Hjalgrim, Christian Erikstrup, Bertram D Kjerulff, Lotte Hindhede, Thomas F Hansen, Mette Nyegaard, Ewan Birney
pmc-11446992.description: Aims/hypothesisMetabolic risk factors and plasma biomarkers for diabetes have previously been shown to change prior to a clinical diabetes diagnosis. However, these markers only cover a small subset of molecular biomarkers linked to the disease. In this study, we aimed to profile a more comprehensive set of molecular biomarkers and explore their temporal association with incident diabetes.

pmc-11513584.title: ESOT Roadmap for Advanced Therapy Medicinal Products in Transplantation: Navigating Regulatory Challenges to Enhance Access and Care
pmc-11513584.creator: Ekaterine Berishvili, Lorenzo Piemonti, Eelco J. P. de Koning, Sandra Lindstedt, Hanne Scholz, William E. Scott, Celine Auxenfans, Paul Johnson, Dominique E. Martin, Penilla Gunther, Devi Mey, Luciano Potena, Olivier Thaunat
pmc-11513584.description: The field of organ transplantation is experiencing a transformative shift with the rise of Advanced Therapy Medicinal Products (ATMPs), which include gene therapies, somatic cell therapies, and tissue-engineered products. These therapies offer new, potentially curative treatments for longstanding medical challenges, impacting numerous patients. However, their adoption is hindered by complex regulatory frameworks, high production costs, and inconsistent access across Europe.

pmc-11525141.title: Breast cancer in adolescents and young adults has a specific biology and poor patient outcome compared with older patients
pmc-11525141.creator: M Oshi, A Yamada, S Gandhi, R Wu, M Sasamoto, S Yamamoto, K Narui, T Ishikawa, K Takabe, I Endo
pmc-11525141.description: BackgroundWe aimed to clarify the features of adolescents and young adults (AYA: younger than 40 years old) breast cancer (BC) compared with other age groups in estrogen receptor (ER)-positive/human epidermal growth factor receptor 2 (HER2)-negative BC, given the effects of age-related hormonal status.

pmc-12418336.title: Ozone-mediated breakdown of microplastics in aqueous environments
pmc-12418336.creator: Markus A. B. Wieland, Sebastian P. Schwaminger, Matthias Elinkmann, Paul M. Stüger, Jörg Feldmann, David Clases, Raquel Gonzalez de Vega
pmc-12418336.description: Advanced oxidation processes (AOPs) are increasingly adopted in wastewater treatment to degrade persistent pollutants, including emerging targets such as microplastics (MPs). These particles enter aquatic systems through the fragmentation of bulk plastics and, as their size decreases, exhibit enhanced mobility, surface reactivity, and biological uptake potential.

pmc-12461325.title: Global Proteome Analysis of a Three-Dimensional Human Chondrocyte Cell Culture System Infected with Chikungunya Virus (CHIKV) Reveals Distinct Immune and Inflammatory Signatures
pmc-12461325.creator: Abdul Hasan, Geetika Sharma, Nilotpal Majumder, Sakshi Chaudhary, Divya Mehta, Raju Vaishya, Sourabh Ghosh, Sujatha Sunil
pmc-12461325.description: Chikungunya disease (CHIKD) presents as an acute viral fever with severe joint pain, which may progress into a chronic arthritic condition that can last for months or even years. The cell tropism of chikungunya virus (CHIKV) infection is well studied; however, the mechanisms underlying the pathogenesis of chronicity, especially in the joints, remain poorly understood.

pmc-13050768.title: Diagnostic approach, vaccination and treatment priorities for Lumpy Skin Disease in cattle: lessons from Balkan epidemics to Western Europe re-emergence (2025)
pmc-13050768.creator: Eda Baldan Toker, Mevlüt Yaşar, Annamaria Pratelli, Kadir Yeşilbağ
pmc-13050768.description: Lumpy skin disease (LSD) remains a high-impact, transboundary infection of cattle driven by capripoxvirus transmission via mechanical vectors, causing morbidity, production losses, and trade disruption. Following the 2015–2017 Balkan epidemics, coordinated high-coverage vaccination campaigns and movement restrictions substantially reduced disease transmission across southeastern Europe.

pmc-13237066.title: Inhibition of TRPC6 channel suppresses bladder cancer proliferation by disrupting store-operated calcium entry
pmc-13237066.creator: Jinhui Zha, Xiaotong Guo, Wentao Liao, Peitao Wu, Yuhong Wu, Yingyue Guo, Weifeng Yang, Li Gao
pmc-13237066.description: Despite its prevalence, bladder cancer (BC) remains an unsolved pathogenesis. It is believed that TRPC6 channels have unique electrophysiological properties that contribute to intracellular Ca2+ signalling and tumorigenesis in cells. However, the mechanism by which TRPC6 contributes to BC progression and intracellular Ca2+ homeostasis remains unclear.

pmc-13368605.title: Assessing the potential of subcutaneous biologging tools for physiological monitoring in a large terrestrial mammal, the Guanaco (Lama guanicoe)
pmc-13368605.creator: Antonella Panebianco, María V Rago, Pablo F Gregorio, Fiama Peña Lodis, Megan A Owen, Valeria Pomponio, María P Pompei, Melina Anello, Natalia M Schroeder, Ramiro Ovejero, Pablo Carmanchahi, Andrea Fuller
pmc-13368605.description: Physiological responses of animals to environmental and anthropogenic stressors are fundamental to effective conservation and wildlife management. Continuous monitoring of heart rate (HR) and body temperature yields key information on energy expenditure, stress, reproduction and health status. However, acquiring long-term physiological data from free-ranging large mammals remains technically challenging.

pmc-13576608.title: Understanding Low Motivation for Treatment in Primary Hyperparathyroidism: A Qualitative Study of Patients and Providers in the United States
pmc-13576608.creator: John O'Connor, Alexandra Helbing, Diana Guiterrez‐Meza, Esra Alagoz, Alexander Chiu
pmc-13576608.description: BackgroundTwo thirds of patients with primary hyperparathyroidism (PHPT) go untreated, risking progressive osteoporosis, fractures, and nephrolithiasis. Low patient motivation for surgery has been identified as a significant factor limiting surgical referral and treatment. We sought to better understand what patient and clinician‐level factors drive low patient motivation to identify targetable interventions.
